title: Weekly release train: cut process, RC tagging, and release-notes automation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a repeatable weekly release train and automated RC-cut workflow for Redwood runtime releases, including RC tagging conventions, release-notes generation, and gating policies for canary rollouts and LTS promotions. Background: we currently make ad-hoc cuts which creates churn for support, inconsistent release notes, and manual gating for canaries. This ticket consolidates the cut checklist, implements CI jobs to create RC tags and draft release notes, wires a Slack notification and release dashboard, and defines rollforward/rollback playbooks. Out of scope: full UI for release creation in Console (follow-up ticket planned).
acceptance_criteria: A weekly CI job creates a candidate RC tag automatically from the main branch on the scheduled cadence
Release notes are generated automatically from merged PR metadata and a curated changelog template and published as a draft to the releases page
Cut process includes automated pre-cut checks: passing smoke e2e, no failing canary alerts, and <0.5% increase in error budget burn during testing window
Canary rollout automation accepts gating signals (SLO, errors, latency) and can pause/rollback without manual intervention
LTS promotion flow requires explicit manual approval and is gated by a stability window and regression metrics
tasks: Draft formal weekly cadence doc: cut window, freeze rules, owner rotation (on-call + release lead)
Implement CI pipeline (github actions) to tag RCs using pattern runtime-{major}.{minor}.{patch}-rc{n}
Build release-notes generator that aggregates PR titles, changelog labels, and manual highlights; output markdown and Confluence entry
Add pre-cut automated checks: e2e-smoke, integration-tests, canary-metrics sanity check
Create canary rollout job in Argo Rollouts / our orchestration layer with metric-based gates
Add manual LTS promotion job with approval step and checklist
Document rollback and emergency cut process in runbook and link to incident playbooks
decisions: Tagging strategy: semantic-major.minor.patch with separate -rc counter to allow multiple candidates per patch; this minimizes user-facing ambiguity while preserving history
Release notes source: PR metadata + changelog labels (chore/bug/feat/regression) with manual highlights section for PM/Eng lead review
Canary gating: rely on platform SLOs (p95 latency, error-rate) emitted to metrics pipeline instead of ad-hoc smoke scripts to keep automation consistent
LTS policy: promote to LTS only after 4 weekly stable releases and explicit SRE signoff to avoid premature promotions

rollout_gates: Automated canary metric gate: p95 latency <= baseline*1.15
Error-rate gate: delta <= 0.5% vs baseline over 30m
Log anomaly detection: no new high-frequency error signatures
Manual hold if any critical customer-facing tests fail
upgrade_tooling_notes: Provide a stable on-disk format checker as part of the release acceptance tests to ensure backward compatibility of KV cache snapshots
Bundle migration helpers into the release artifact and surface a --dry-run mode in the upgrade CLI
Add a rollback toggle in the CLI that resets symlinked runtime binaries and restores previous configuration snapshot
Ensure private/VPC upgrade paths are compatible with the new RC tagging to simplify customer patch workflows
notes_on_lts: LTS channel defined as a quarterly promoted train after 4 consecutive weekly stable releases
LTS promotion requires SRE signoff and automated regression check suite to pass
Security patches on LTS can be backported and released as runtime-{major}.{minor}.x-rc{n} with expedited approval
